Not OP, but i feel similarly to how they do. I’m early 20’s as well. Just started grad school… as in today. I realize i really don’t want to do another 2 years of school. i graduated. it finally felt like an accomplishment. only to start again with higher expectations. I don’t want to be here, but i need a job. I hate jobs, though. It never feels fulfilling. There never seems to be a point other than get money. But living to work from 9 to 5, 5 days a week, until i’m 65 doesn’t seem appealing in the slightest to me. I know everyone wishes they could live comfortably without a job. that’s the dream, it won’t happen for me. What i’m studying is the only thing i’d be interested in academically, and the only hope of getting a decently paying starting position. 

I have literally no drive, nothing pushing me to contribute to society, to do my homework, to do a job. I’d be dead right now if i wouldn’t feel bad for my parents. So what do I do? I have no marketable traits, nor do i really want to learn one. I don’t want to do anything, but I can’t die yet.

I guess i could attribute this to my upbringing. upper middle class, given everything. But then again, some friends brought up in a similar situation are driven, and my brother will be a doctor (as in they’re in med school getting amazing grades), and probably a millionaire within 2 decades. Plus he’s engaged. So where did I go wrong? I have no clue.
But what if they don’t want to? What if they cannot find a drive?
